questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to breathe properly when you are stressed
Why mice have fast hearts
Why we sigh and how sighing keeps us alive
How to reset a computer
questions.why: Dan says they'll look at why we sigh and learn how sighing keeps us alive.

questions.q: Was Catherine's sigh at the start of the show real?
options: No, it was just to show what a sigh is
Yes, she was tired
Yes, she was frustrated with Dan
Yes, she was relieved
questions.why: Catherine says that one 'was just for educational purposes'.

questions.q: According to Dr Lynne Barker, what would happen to people who didn't sigh?
options: They would sleep badly
They would feel more stressed
They would breathe more slowly
They would eventually die
questions.why: She says 'people who don't sigh would eventually die. It is a survival mechanism.'

questions.q: What did scientists at UCLA find about sighing?
options: It makes the heart beat faster and raises blood pressure
It is a deep breath that keeps the lungs' tiny air sacs working
It removes water and dust from deep inside the lungs
It only happens when we're feeling sad, tired or lonely
questions.why: They found a sigh is a special deep breath that keeps the alveoli in our lungs working properly.

options: Because she saw a mouse
To show Dan an example of a reflex
Because Dan made a mistake
To wake up the listeners
questions.why: After Dan jumps, she says 'that was a fabulous reflex', something done without thinking.

questions.q: When does Catherine say she sighs?
options: When she is bored or hungry
When she is angry
Only when she exercises
When she is tired or relieved
questions.why: Catherine says she sighs when she's tired and when she's relieved.

questions.q: What example of relief does Catherine give?
options: Her friend recovered from a serious illness last year
Her boss finally listened to her ideas at a meeting
She found her new phone that she thought she'd lost
She passed an important exam she thought she'd failed
questions.why: She breathed a sigh of relief when she found her new phone, which she thought she'd lost.

questions.q: Why does Dan tend to sigh?
options: To show frustration or that he accepts something bad
Because he is often tired after working late at night
Because he is happy and wants others to know it
Only when he is surprised by some unexpected news
questions.why: Dan says he tends to sigh to show frustration, and sometimes resignation.
